title: Compliance Messaging Playbook: SOC2 / HIPAA / ISO Positioning (Draft)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working playbook for go-to-market messaging around Redwood Inference's security and compliance posture. Primary audiences: sales reps (technical + enterprise), solutions engineers, product marketing, and legal for review. Secondary: customer success and docs. Status: draft — some language needs legal sign-off (see open questions).

High-level positioning statement (for lead gen / one-pager):
- Headline: Production-grade inference with enterprise controls — SOC 2, ISO-ready processes, HIPAA options for protected data.
- Subhead: Deliver LLM features at scale without trading off security or auditability. Our platform combines hardened infrastructure, fine-grained controls, and transparent audit logs so engineering teams can meet compliance requirements while optimizing cost and latency.

Core claim guidance (short, compliant snippets for website/one-pager):
- "SOC 2 controls implemented across our control plane and operational processes; annual third-party assessment planned."
- "ISO 27001-aligned policies and gap plan for formal certification in 2026 Q3."
- "HIPAA: Business Associate Agreement (BAA) available for customers with protected health data; private deployment options for on-prem/VPC environments."
- "Audit logs: immutable, retention-configurable audit trails for request metadata, model version, and reviewer actions."

Note: Avoid absolute language like "SOC 2 certified" or "ISO certified" until audit complete. Use words like "SOC 2 controls" or "ISO-aligned" if certification is pending.

Detailed messaging blocks for sales & SEs:
1) Enterprise intro (60s pitch):
   - "Redwood makes inference predictable and auditable. For regulated customers we offer a hardened private control plane, optional on-prem deployments, and audit-grade logging. We can sign a BAA and provide documentation for SOC-aligned controls and data handling practices."
2) Technical SE snippet (2–3 bullets):
   - "Per-request metadata capture: user id, request id, model variant, region, inference latency, and cost metrics."
   - "Immutable storage for audit logs with configurable retention and export to customer SIEM (S3, GCS, or Kinesis)."
   - "Data handling controls: ephemeral KV caches, optional zero-retention option for hosted requests, and deterministic redaction hooks for PII before persistence."
3) Objection handling / FAQ (short answers):
   - Q: "Are you SOC 2 / ISO / HIPAA certified?"
     A: "We operate SOC 2-aligned controls and maintain ISO-aligned policies; formal certifications/assessments are tracked in our compliance roadmap and available on request. For HIPAA workloads we sign a BAA and recommend private deployments for highest isolation."
   - Q: "How do you prevent sensitive data from being used for model training?"
     A: "We do not use customer production data to train models; model updates follow a controlled ingestion pipeline and require explicit approvals from our model operations team. Customers can opt into fully isolated model variants or host models inside a private deployment."
   - Q: "Can we export raw logs for audits?"
     A: "Yes — audit logs can be exported to customer-owned buckets or streamed to SIEMs. We support hashing/obfuscation for sensitive fields prior to export per contract requirements."

Competitive notes (how to differentiate vs public LLM APIs and other inference platforms):
- Public LLM providers: Strength = simplicity. Risk = limited contractual BAA options and less operational transparency (e.g., token-level cost + latency). Messaging: emphasize our auditability, private deployments, and rolling policies that align to customer SLAs.
- Self-hosted inference vendors: Strength = control. Weakness = ops burden. Messaging: highlight Redwood’s unified control plane, managed auditability, and migration path from hosted to private/dedicated (minimize rebuild).
- Enterprise cloud AI offerings: Strength = compliance pedigree. Weakness = inference economics and model flexibility. Messaging: emphasize cost/performance controls (batching, caching, quantization) + first-class routing/fallbacks to maintain reliability in regulated setups.

Audit-log language (wording for contracts, product pages, and docs):
- "Audit logs capture request-level metadata, model variant, user and service identities, timestamps, and operator actions. Logs are stored in an immutable store and can be retained per customer-defined retention policies. Logs are exportable to customer-managed storage or SIEM integrations (S3/GCS/Kinesis)."
- "Redwood maintains role-based access controls for log access; access events to audit stores are themselves logged and subject to periodic review."

Data handling and retention bullets (technical/legal checklist):
- Clearly separate: transit vs persistence vs caching.
- Transit: TLS 1.2+ (prefer TLS 1.3), mutual TLS available for Private deployments.
- Persistence: Request payloads are not persisted by default in hosted mode; configurable retention window for debugging. Private deployments default to customer-managed persistence.
- Caching: KV cache is in-memory with eviction, optional encryption at rest for private/dedicated GPUs.
- Backups: Encrypted backups of control-plane metadata only; payload backups require explicit contract.

Sample audit controls mapping (for SOC 2 / ISO conversations):
- Logging & monitoring: request logs, operator actions, incident timelines.
- Access controls: RBAC, SSO (SAML/SAML2.0, OIDC) integrations, least privilege admin roles.
- Change management: controlled rollout process, canary flags, rollback, PR-linked change records for model/version updates.
- Vendor/third-party: list of cloud providers, hardware vendors, and crypto/KMS providers; third-party assessments in progress.

Open questions / legal checks (to resolve before external use):
- Can we say "SOC 2 controls implemented" in public marketing without context? Legal to confirm specific phrasing.
- Exact scope for BAA (which hosted plans qualify) and whether Hosted API can be BAA-covered or only Private/Dedicated.
- Export templates for log delivery (format, retention, PII obfuscation).
- ISO certification timeline: internal milestones vs externally communicated target date.

Quick go-to-market assets to produce from this doc (owners suggested):
- One-pager: "Security & Compliance at Redwood" (PMM) — target: web and sales deck (owner: Priya).
- Sales play: objection-handling cheat sheet (SE friendly) (owner: Marcus).
- Technical doc: "Audit logs + exports" with endpoints, schema, retention config (owner: Ava).
- Legal: BAA template and scope memo (owner: Samira).

Appendix: suggested short-lines for hero sections, product tiles, and email outreach:
- For hero: "Audit-grade inference for regulated apps — SOC2-aligned controls, BAA, and private deployments."
- Product tile (hosting): "Hosted API with optional zero-retention mode and log export."
- Product tile (dedicated/private): "Dedicated GPU pools, VPC + on-prem options, and customer-controlled audit trails."
- Cold outreach line: "We help teams ship LLM features that meet SOC2 and HIPAA requirements without the ops overhead — can I connect you with our security SE for a 20-min walkthrough?"

Notes to self (author):
- Keep file in go-to-market root and iterate with legal & infra. Pull audit-log schema from infra repo PR #1123 (linked above).
- Follow up meeting scheduled 2026-03-12 with Legal + Infra to finalize BAA scope.
- Next revision should include sample screenshots of Console audit log UI and sample export file (JSON schema).

End of draft.
